overviewHtml:
This ungraded knowledge check assesses your understanding of what changes when an AI system acts for you over many steps. You'll be asked about what agents do unattended, permissions and excessive agency, prompt injection and the lethal trifecta, and checkpoints and reversibility.

Note: Use this to test yourself, review the feedback on any questions you miss, and retry until you feel confident before moving forward.

forms.stemHtml: An agent misreads a date at the second step of a fifteen-step task, and every later step proceeds from the wrong date. What is this kind of failure called?

options.html: Excessive agency, since the agent had too much access
options.text: Excessive agency, since the agent had too much access
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Excessive agency concerns what an agent is able to reach and do. A mistake at one step that later steps build on is a compounding error.

options.html: Prompt injection, since a wrong instruction got in
options.text: Prompt injection, since a wrong instruction got in
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Prompt injection involves instructions from someone else. Here the agent made its own mistake, and later steps built on it, which is a compounding error.

options.html: A compounding error, since later steps built on it
options.text: A compounding error, since later steps built on it
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A compounding error is a mistake at one step that later steps build on, so its effects grow. Longer tasks give an early mistake more room to carry forward.

options.html: An unattended step, since nobody saw it take place
options.text: An unattended step, since nobody saw it take place
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. An unattended step is any step you don't see as it happens, whether or not it goes wrong. A mistake that later steps build on is a compounding error.

forms.stemHtml: You want an AI agent to summarize the documents in one project folder. Which grant follows least privilege?

options.html: Read and write access to the whole shared drive
options.text: Read and write access to the whole shared drive
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. A summary needs neither write access nor the whole drive. Least privilege means read access to the one folder.

options.html: Write access to the one project folder only
options.text: Write access to the one project folder only
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Summarizing doesn't require changing anything, so write access adds risk and no benefit. Least privilege means read access to the one folder.

options.html: Read access to the whole shared drive
options.text: Read access to the whole shared drive
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The scope is wider than the task needs. Least privilege means read access to the one folder.

options.html: Read access to the one project folder only
options.text: Read access to the one project folder only
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Least privilege grants only what the task needs: viewing, and only the folder in question.

forms.stemHtml: Which of these are the three legs of the lethal trifecta? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Access to private data
options.text: Access to private data
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Private data is what an attacker would be after.

options.html: Exposure to untrusted content
options.text: Exposure to untrusted content
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Content written by someone else is how a hidden instruction reaches the agent.

options.html: A way to communicate externally
options.text: A way to communicate externally
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! An outside channel is how data would be carried away.

options.html: A task with more than ten steps
options.text: A task with more than ten steps
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Task length affects how errors carry forward, and it isn't part of the trifecta. The three legs are private data, untrusted content, and outside communication.

options.html: A model can't reliably tell your instructions from text it reads
options.text: A model can't reliably tell your instructions from text it reads
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A model receives your request and the content it reads as one stream of text, and nothing reliably marks which parts came from you.

options.html: A model gives more weight to web pages than to its own user
options.text: A model gives more weight to web pages than to its own user
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The problem isn't a ranking of sources. A model can't reliably tell your instructions from text it's reading, so it may follow either.

options.html: A model is designed to obey whichever instruction came last
options.text: A model is designed to obey whichever instruction came last
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Order isn't the cause. A model can't reliably tell your instructions from text it's reading, so it may follow either.

options.html: A model stores hidden instructions from earlier conversations with you
options.text: A model stores hidden instructions from earlier conversations with you
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The instructions arrive in content the model reads during the task. A model can't reliably tell your instructions from that text, so it may follow either.

forms.stemHtml: An agent prepares a monthly expense report and submits it for payment. Where does an approval step matter most?

options.html: Before the agent opens the folder of receipts
options.text: Before the agent opens the folder of receipts
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Opening a folder changes nothing and can be repeated. The approval step matters most before the report is submitted for payment, which can't easily be undone.

options.html: Before the agent submits the report for payment
options.text: Before the agent submits the report for payment
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Submitting for payment is hard to undo. An approval step there means an agent's mistake stays a draft.

options.html: Before the agent adds up the totals in a draft
options.text: Before the agent adds up the totals in a draft
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. A draft total can be corrected at no cost. The approval step matters most before the report is submitted for payment, which can't easily be undone.

options.html: Before the agent saves a copy of the draft report
options.text: Before the agent saves a copy of the draft report
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Saving a copy is reversible. The approval step matters most before the report is submitted for payment, which can't easily be undone.

title: Delegating to agents and keeping oversight
